title: Drag and drop
learningObjectives: Explain drag and drop and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: HTML drag-and-drop uses events such as dragstart, dragover, drop, and dragend. A drop target generally needs to call preventDefault during dragover to allow dropping. The DataTransfer object carries transferred data and files.
understand.whyItMatters: Drag-and-drop should not be the only way to complete an action. Provide keyboard-accessible alternatives and validate dropped files or data just like file-input selections.
understand.analogy: Drag-and-drop is one way to hand an item to a target; a keyboard or button action should offer another route.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: preventDefault allows the drop operation. The example reads file names only; content must be validated before processing.

examples.explanation: preventDefault allows the drop operation. The example reads file names only; content must be validated before processing.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Build a drop zone and a normal file picker that share the same validation function. Test keyboard use without dragging.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: Which event commonly needs preventDefault to allow a drop target?
questions.explanation: Preventing the default dragover action enables the element to accept a drop.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach when using browser APIs?
options: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.answer: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.explanation: Browser features need graceful fallback, privacy-aware permission, and lifecycle management.
